<thought>Based on the observed isotopic pattern—a prominent M+2 peak at ~4.6 % of the base peak (consistent with the natural abundance of 34S) and a very small M+4 peak (~0.06 % matching the low abundance of 36S)—the presence of sulfur can be definitively concluded. No other element shows a characteristic isotopic spacing or relative intensity that allows a definitive identification from this spectrum alone.</thought>
<final_answer>['S']</final_answer>
